findings.name: Tax Credit for Service-Connected Total Disability
findings.description: New Hampshire provides a standard $700 annual property tax credit on the principal residence of a veteran who was honorably discharged and is rated totally and permanently disabled from a service-connected condition, or is a double amputee or paraplegic from a service-connected injury (or the surviving spouse of such a veteran). Individual cities and towns may vote to adopt a higher local credit ranging from $701 up to $5,000, which then replaces the standard credit entirely. Applicants must provide VA certification of total and permanent service-connected disability; the credit applies only to the applicant's principal residence.
findings.value: $700 standard annual property tax credit; municipalities may adopt $701-$5,000 in its place
otherReqs: Honorable discharge required
Totally and permanently disabled from service connection, OR double amputee/paraplegic from service-connected injury
Applies only to principal residence
VA certification of total and permanent service-connected disability required
findings.agency: NH Department of Revenue Administration / Municipal Assessor
findings.form: PA-29 (Permanent Application for Property Tax Credit/Exemption)
documentation: VA certification of total and permanent service-connected disability
DD-214 or proof of honorable discharge
findings.sourceExcerpt: $700 of property taxes on the person's residential property annually for eligible veterans with service-connected total disability. Cities and towns may adopt an alternative credit of $701 up to $5,000 under RSA 72:27-a. Applicants must provide certification from the United States Department of Veterans' Affairs that the applicant is rated totally and permanently disabled from service connection.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate Fee Exemption
findings.description: New Hampshire exempts veterans with a permanent and total (P&T) VA disability rating from the $50 vehicle license fee. Veterans who are amputees, paraplegic, or blind are also exempt from vehicle registration fees when the vehicle was provided by the VA. Vehicles bearing disabled veteran license plates receive free parking time in any New Hampshire city or town while under the direct control of the owner. Applicants bring VA proof of disability and a DD-214 to any DMV office or Town/City Clerk's office that processes registrations.
findings.value: Exempt from $50 license fee (P&T rating); exempt from registration fees for VA-provided vehicles (amputee/paraplegic/blind veterans); free municipal parking
otherReqs: Permanent and Total (P&T) VA disability rating for the license fee exemption
Amputee, paraplegic, or blind status with VA-provided vehicle for the registration fee exemption
DD-214 and VA proof of disability required at application
findings.sourceExcerpt: Veterans with a P&T VA disability rating are exempt from the $50 license fee. Veterans who are amputees, paraplegic, or blind are exempt from vehicle registration fees when the vehicle is provided by the VA. Any motor vehicle bearing special disabled veteran license plates shall be allowed free parking time in any city or town if the vehicle is under the direct control of the owner.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran Lifetime Hunting/Fishing License
findings.description: New Hampshire residents who received a discharge other than dishonorable and are totally and permanently disabled from a service-connected disability are eligible for a free perpetual lifetime license (fishing, hunting, or bow and arrow) for a one-time $10 administrative fee. Veterans with at least an 80% but less than 100% VA disability rating for at least two years may purchase a lifetime license at half price. Documentation must show the permanent disability rating and honorable discharge status, and a Department review (up to 5 business days) is required before the license is issued.
findings.value: Free lifetime license for $10 one-time fee (100% P&T); half-price lifetime license (80-99% for 2+ years)
otherReqs: Discharge other than dishonorable
100% totally and permanently disabled tier: free license for $10 admin fee
80-99% disability rating held for at least 2 years: half-price lifetime license
Department review of application required (up to 5 business days)
findings.agency: New Hampshire Fish and Game Department
findings.form: Disabled Veterans Resident Lifetime License Application
documentation: VA documentation of permanent disability rating
Proof of honorable (or other than dishonorable) discharge
findings.sourceExcerpt: Honorably discharged resident veterans who have a service-connected, total and permanent disability rating from the VA are eligible for free lifetime licenses, with only a $10 administrative fee charged once when applying. Veterans who have at least an 80% but not 100% disability rating from the VA for at least two years may purchase a lifetime license for half price.

findings.name: Community College Tuition Waiver for Children of Disabled Veterans and MIA/POW Dependents
findings.description: Under RSA 188-F:15, a child of a veteran who received an honorable discharge and is 100% permanently disabled from a service-connected injury (and who was a New Hampshire resident when entering service or at the time of disability determination) is not required to pay tuition at a Community College System of New Hampshire institution. The same waiver applies to a child of a New Hampshire-domiciled service member reported missing in action or captured during the Southeast Asian conflict, enrolled after March 23, 1972. "Child" includes biological, adopted, and stepchildren meeting residency standards, and eligibility runs through the semester the child turns 27. Applicants must complete the FAFSA and pursue other available financial aid (excluding VA education benefits) and may need to document the veteran's disability status and their relationship to the veteran.
findings.value: Full tuition waiver at Community College System of New Hampshire institutions
otherReqs: Veteran received an honorable discharge and is 100% permanently disabled from a service-connected injury, OR was declared MIA/POW during the Southeast Asian conflict while NH-domiciled
Veteran was a NH resident when entering service or at disability determination
Child eligible through the semester they turn 27
Must file FAFSA and pursue other financial aid (excluding VA education benefits)
findings.agency: Community College System of New Hampshire
documentation: VA documentation of veteran's 100% permanent service-connected disability, or MIA/POW documentation
Proof of relationship to the veteran
findings.sourceExcerpt: Any child of such person enrolled in an institution that is part of the community college system of New Hampshire shall not be required to pay tuition if the veteran received an honorable discharge, is 100% permanently disabled from service-connected injury, and meets residency requirements. Children remain eligible through the semester they turn 27.

findings.name: State and Public Employment Veterans' Preference
findings.description: New Hampshire law grants hiring preference to citizens who served in the U.S. Armed Forces for not less than 90 days during wartime and were honorably discharged (or released from active duty), for public employment positions such as clerks, office help, mechanics, laborers, inspectors, supervisors, foremen, janitors, and peace officers, in state and municipal departments and public works, when the veteran is equally qualified and registered per RSA 283:7. Additional statutory preference applies to appointments within the State Liquor Commission, the Division of Veterans Services, and the New Hampshire Veterans Home.
findings.value: Hiring preference for equally-qualified wartime veterans in state/municipal public employment
otherReqs: Served not less than 90 days during wartime
Honorably discharged or released from active duty
Registered per RSA 283:7
Preference applies only when the veteran is equally qualified to other applicants
findings.agency: New Hampshire Department of Labor / NH Division of Veterans Services
documentation: DD-214 or proof of honorable discharge/wartime service
findings.sourceExcerpt: In public employment of clerks, office help, mechanics, laborers, inspectors, supervisors, foremen, janitors, peace officers... preference shall be given to citizens of the state who have served in the armed forces of the United States, for not less than 90 days, in times of war, and have been discharged honorably therefrom or released from active duty therein, if equally qualified for said employment and if registered in accordance with the provisions of RSA 283:7.

findings.name: New Hampshire Veterans Home
findings.description: The New Hampshire Veterans Home in Tilton is a 250-bed, state-operated facility for honorably discharged veterans who served in time of war and have been New Hampshire residents for one year preceding application, or who were NH residents when they entered military service. The Home has served veterans for more than 135 years and provides long-term care with dignity, honor, and respect.
findings.value: Long-term care at a 250-bed state veterans home
otherReqs: Honorable discharge and wartime service
NH residency for one year preceding application, or NH residency at time of entering military service
findings.agency: New Hampshire Veterans Home (State of New Hampshire)
documentation: DD-214 or proof of honorable wartime service
